articles.title: Context Scaling: A New Frontier of AI Scaling
articles.raw_summary: Many failures of deployed AI arise not from weak inference but from a mismatch between the state a task depends on and the context available when the system acts. Relevant user state, repository revisions, tool traces, sensor readings, or environment changes may be unavailable, distorted, or poorly selected. We call the effort to reduce this bottleneck context scaling. We frame a model as $P_\theta(d\mid c)$ within a system governed by three budgets: training $B_\theta$, decision-time $B_d$, and context-infrastructure $B_c$. Pretraining scaling invests in $\theta$; decision-time scaling search

articles.title: Constraint-Aware Test-Time Scoring for LLM and VLM Candidate Selection
articles.raw_summary: When an LLM or VLM produces several candidate answers, picking the best one usually relies on the model's own confidence, a learned judge model, or a domain check. Each has a known weakness: an answer can be fluent but insecure, mathematically plausible but physically infeasible, or rated highly by a judge while quietly breaking a task requirement. articles.title: AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics
articles.raw_summary: AI systems are increasingly capable of producing machine-checked Lean proofs of advanced mathematical results. Real mathematical formalization, however, is not isolated theorem proving: it requires building the definitions and intermediate lemmas that connect a result to a formal library. articles.title: General-Purpose Decision Models for AI Configuration Tuning
articles.raw_summary: AI configuration tuning searches for settings that improve the performance of AI systems under a limited budget. Existing tuners use different sampling and search policies, making the choice of decision strategy central to both tuning quality and cost. We investigate whether general-purpose decision models can guide tuning, using Jev as a deployed representative that returns structured choices and numeric scores across diverse tasks. articles.title: What, Who, and When: Structured Harm Assessment for Mental Health Safety via Short Reasoning
articles.raw_summary: The growing use of large language models (LLMs) for mental health support raises important safety concerns. Existing guard models primarily identify categories of harmful content, often overlooking the context needed to determine an appropriate response. We introduce a clinically grounded taxonomy that characterizes harm along three dimensions: what the harm is, who is involved, and when it occurs. articles.title: Certify What You Plant: Shortcut-Free Proof Depth in Logical Reasoning Data
articles.raw_summary: Procedurally generated logic problems are used to both evaluate and train reasoning in language models.
